The plan and deliveries. I need to see what will be left after deliveries.
No turns in this track, yet that's the same birch again. Something strange going on.
District paperwork. They write about the fields. We're the ones who have to plow them.
Something strange is happening... We haven't turned off anywhere.
It won't just be neighbors I have to hear out through that door.
Something's not right. We haven't turned, but that's the same birch.
Our whole farm on one sheet. I know the land well enough.
Something very strange. The route is correct. We haven't taken any turns.
New posters, same old wall underneath.
Devil take it. Straight ahead all the way, and that birch again.
The first letter is the plan from the district. I'm the one who'll have to answer it.
Now, wait a moment. This is getting rather strange. The same birch, and we haven't turned.
Can't keep everything in my head. Best write things down too.
Something's not right. The horse senses it too.
New names in the newspaper. I don't know any of these people.
I'll put the seeds away from the stove. They can stay here for now.
I don't recognize the General Secretary. Nothing's been right since that fog... Where have I ended up?
April, thirty-one. Spring won't wait.
The pendulum's swinging. At least something moves when you're sitting here alone.

Locked. I won't force it.

Not much snow, and the water drained away quickly. That's why the road holds. An ordinary spring, we'd be stuck up to the axle.
Paperwork from the district. Wishing won't get us machinery.
Little snow this winter, little meltwater. So the ground holds. In an ordinary year, we wouldn't have got here so easily.
People will come to see me here. Let them tell me what's stopping the work.
A winter with little snow saved this road. Most springs, you can't get through to the district. No use counting on quick help then.
Fields here, roads there. I'll need to think through hauling.

They've put up a poster. Now to get the farm running too.
Little snow this winter. That's why we got through. Most springs, any wagon train would be sunk to the hubs here.

A district newspaper, but the names mean nothing to me.
Brought my tools. At least I won't have to borrow a screwdriver.

Noisy rooks, and a chapel over there. An old village. I'll have to take local customs into account.

Good conditions. So the land alone doesn't explain the ruin.
A hand-drawn map. I'll still have to check the boundaries on the ground.

I'd better read this more carefully. Not a single familiar name.
The briefcase is worn, but the lock's sound. It'll serve a while yet.

Correspondence with the district. Familiar procedures, on paper at least.

A single bridge for the whole connection to the district. There's the first risk.
A map of the farm. I'll learn the terrain before reporting on it.
The only crossing. I'll need to coordinate repairs with the district at once.

Contacts and reminders. Best not rely on memory alone.

Paperwork from the district. Even an order needs reading first here.

They'll be waiting here. So I'd better be at my post.
Abandoned land all along the road. This wasn't one failed sowing. They've let the field go for years.

New names. Didn't hear of any of them on the way.

District correspondence. Useful to know what they want of me.

District paperwork. I'll see what needs doing now and what can wait.
